topic: DP-3T: The Privacy-Preserving Shield for Contact Tracing
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Cybersecurity) and tech-savvy professionals

sections.title: The Privacy Dilemma: Public Health vs. Personal Secret
lecture_lines: Traditional contact tracing often risks personal privacy.
Centralized servers track your location and identity.
DP-3T offers a privacy-first, decentralized alternative.
animations: Virus icon (#FF4500) spreads through a network of white circles.
Large 'Eye' icon (#FFFFFF) appears above the network, collecting data.
Transition to a 'Shield' icon (#00FF7F) protecting the user nodes.

sections.title: Prerequisite 1: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) & Hashing
lecture_lines: Bluetooth Low Energy enables short-range digital handshakes.
Cryptographic hashing turns secret keys into random IDs.
These one-way functions prevent reversing the random IDs.
animations: Two phone icons emit blue concentric rings (#1E90FF) for BLE.
A 'Secret Key' text (#FFD700) enters a 'Hash Box' (#A9A9A9).
A 'Unique ID' string (#ADFF2F) exits the 'Hash Box'.

sections.title: The Daily Cycle: Generating Ephemeral IDs (EphID)
lecture_lines: Every day, your phone generates a Secret Day Key.
From this key, it derives multiple Ephemeral IDs.
These random IDs change every fifteen minutes.
Frequent rotation prevents anyone from tracking your device.
Your true identity remains hidden behind these IDs.
animations: Show 'Secret Day Key' ($SK_t$) as a gold node (#FFD700).
Generate multiple 'EphID' nodes (#87CEEB) branching from the key.
A clock icon (#FFFFFF) ticks, indicating time passing.
Highlight one EphID; previous one fades out each tick.
'Attacker' icon (#FF0000) tries and fails to link EphIDs.

sections.title: The Encounter: Recording the Digital Handshake
lecture_lines: When phones meet, they exchange rotating Ephemeral IDs.
Your phone records the signal strength and ID.
This data is stored locally on your device only.
No location or personal information is ever exchanged.
The central server knows nothing about this meeting.
animations: Alice and Bob icons (#00BFFF, #FF69B4) move close together.
Packet 'ID_A1' moves to Bob; 'ID_B1' moves to Alice.
'Local Diary' icon (#F5DEB3) appears on both phones, storing IDs.
Ghostly 'GPS' and 'Identity' icons (#A9A9A9) appear with red strike-throughs.
A 'Server' icon (#808080) at the screen edge appears grayed out and disconnected.

sections.title: The Infection Report: Uploading the Secret Key
lecture_lines: If infected, users voluntarily upload their Secret Day Keys.
Only the keys are sent to the central server.
The server never receives contact lists or locations.
animations: Bob icon turns red (#FF0000) and selects 14 'Secret Day Keys' (#FFD700).
Keys (#FFD700) move to 'Cloud Server' (#F0F8FF) and then to a 'Public Bulletin Board' (#F5F5DC).
Red 'X' marks over 'Contacts' and 'GPS' icons (#A9A9A9) to show exclusion.

sections.title: The Local Match: Privacy-First Verification
lecture_lines: Phones download new Secret Day Keys from the server.
Your device reconstructs the infected person's rotating IDs.
It checks these IDs against its own local diary.
A match triggers a notification on your device.
The matching process happens entirely on your phone.
animations: Alice icon downloads 'Secret Keys' (#FFD700) from the server.
Alice's phone icon processes keys through a hash function box.
A list of 'Reconstructed IDs' (#87CEEB) fills the screen.
Compare 'Reconstructed IDs' with Alice's 'Local Diary' (#F5DEB3).
A match highlights in yellow (#FFFF00) and triggers 'Risk Alert'.

sections.title: Summary: Why DP-3T Wins
lecture_lines: DP-3T protects identity through decentralized key rotation.
Privacy is maintained by processing matches locally.
Public health and personal secrets can coexist safely.
animations: Central Server icon becomes a simple 'Mailbox' (#B22222).
User icons remain anonymous behind green shields (#00FF7F).
Text 'DP-3T: Public Health + Privacy' appears in white (#FFFFFF).
